blocks.text: Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs) provide standardized guidance to health professionals on the diagnosis and management of various medical conditions. They serve as an essential tool for promoting rational use of medicines and ensuring consistent, evidence-based clinical practice across different levels of the health system. The guidelines also provide critical support to healthcare practitioners, particularly those with limited experience or those newly entering clinical practice. STGs are systematically developed recommendations intended to assist practitioners and prescribers in making appropriate decisions regarding the management of specific clinical conditions.

runs.text: provide critical support to healthcare practitioners, particularly those with limited experience or those newly entering clinical practice. STGs are systematically developed recommendations intended to assist practitioners and prescribers in making appropriate decisions regarding the management of specific clinical conditions.

blocks.text: The guidelines include information on disease conditions, diagnostic criteria, Pharmacological Management which involve the medicines of choice and alternative treatment options, Non-Pharmacological Management, as well as key prescribing information such as dosage, duration of treatment, contraindications, side effects, warnings, medicine interactions, and referral criteria. To remain relevant and responsive to advances in medical science and evolving public health priorities, the STGs are reviewed and updated regularly. In Tanzania, the review process is conducted every three (3) years. The Seventh Edition (2026) of the Standard Treatment Guidelines has been comprehensively revised to incorporate new therapeutic interventions, updated diagnostic approaches, and guidance for the management of emerging and re-emerging diseases.

blocks.text: During the development process, strong emphasis was placed on the application of evidence-based medicine. Each chapter was reviewed and updated by a Lead Reviewer, a recognized expert in the respective disease area, nominated by professional associations, with assistance from a multidisciplinary team of technical experts.
